gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: The witness ___ the police that he knew nothing.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody that... — the personal object 'the police' requires told, not said.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'Hand in your phones,' the invigilator instructed. The invigilator instructed us ___ in our phones.
gaps.explanation: Formal commands: instruct + object + to-infinitive; the particle 'in' stays with the verb.
Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

gaps.sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.
